raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, so I cannot spread myself too thin. I still keep wheat and maize on most of the land because that is the steady way here. Wheat gives us grain and cash, and after wheat I can put in maize quickly on the same ground. Cotton can make money in a good year, but it takes more watching and more picking, so I will only keep a small piece for it. I have no big money to gamble with. I do mostly what worked before. If I skip fertilizer, the land shows it right away, so I will still put some on, but not too much because cash is tight and water from the well costs money too.

For wheat, I will plant on 2 mu in early October like usual. I use the seed people around here buy, not anything fancy, and I put base fertilizer before sowing, then another bit when the wheat starts standing up strong in spring if the leaves look pale. Wheat needs water, so I will likely irrigate 3 times if the rain is not enough. After harvest in June, I will not waste time. The wheat stubble land goes straight into maize, same 2 mu, because the window is short. I usually just do simple tillage and sow fast. For cotton, I keep 1 mu. Cotton can earn more if the year is good, but it needs more hand work, especially picking, and my family also has people working outside, so I cannot make cotton too big.
